notes: PROVISIONAL workload routing metadata. This file decides only WHICH MODEL FITS A WORKLOAD and, within a workload, which centrally validated reasoning controls to send. It grants no permission: every model named here must still clear the independent qualification gate in config/inference_policy.json (dated approval, operator review, verified availability, pinned https endpoint, pinned ZDR transport block, account-side logging disabled, free-model training opt-out, pinned price ceilings, declared model_capabilities and token limits) and must still fit the account's resolved entitlements, budget and context bounds before it can be dispatched. model_routing.json contains no prices, no approvals and no capability grants; commercial.json remains the only source of account capabilities and limits. The routine, background and research profiles are the one measured exception, and only inside a narrow envelope: the 28 September 2026 follow-up screen recorded 16/16 human-acceptable held-out answers for openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna at low effort with no premium semantic advantage, which supports that single automatic candidate and nothing beyond the bounded routine, tool and source-synthesis tasks it was actually shown. Every other placement below, including the reasoning and council pool orderings, the per-profile minimum output budgets and the per-model reasoning presets, remains an UNMEASURED PLACEMENT PENDING REAL EVALUATION: an engineering hypothesis about which model is good enough for which task, not quality evidence. A generic capability flag (text/tools/json_schema) is a protocol fact and never implies answer quality, so a cheap model is only ever chosen because it sits in the first ACCEPTABLE group for that workload, never because it is cheap. Nothing here is fetched at runtime: the model catalogue is not consulted, a model name is never evidence of qualification, and an unlisted model is not routable by profile. Escalation groups exist so a demanding workload has a bounded, ordered, budget-aware path to a stronger model; the bound is the group list, so there is no unbounded premium climb. The routine, background and research profiles deliberately carry no fallback group at all: one accepted automatic candidate each means an unavailable or ineligible Luna is a truthful unavailable/capacity result rather than a silent substitution, and admitting another automatic alternative requires its own evaluation and approval.

models.notes: Provisional cheap tier placement. It deliberately has no generic medium effort: the supported ladder is max/high/low, so a blanket medium would be an unsupported parameter. Suitability is unmeasured and must be re-placed after a real evaluation.

Provisional cheap tier placement and a second cheap developer, so a council round is not pinned to one vendor; it is no longer an automatic candidate for routine, background or research work. No generic medium effort, for the same ladder reason as the DeepSeek flash placement.

Provisional economical candidate and the single accepted automatic candidate for the routine, background and research profiles, at its low default effort. That placement rests on 16/16 human-acceptable held-out answers inside one narrow bounded screen; it is not evidence for memory helpers, general reasoning, coding or demanding work. Its supported effort ladder includes medium; effort support is not a quality ranking, and the council preset and the reasoning/council placements are unchanged.
Provisional cheap tier placement and a fourth distinct developer. It supports medium but not max or xhigh, so the loader rejects any preset outside its declared ladder.
Council diversity placement only: a fifth developer, offered so a council round can spend a perspective outside the DeepSeek, GLM, OpenAI and Google set. It is not a routine or background candidate.

Provisional demanding tier placement in the reasoning and council profiles. It is no longer an automatic candidate for routine, background or research work: those profiles refuse the request rather than degrade to a demanding model. No generic medium effort.

Operator-selected Sol 6.1 replacement at high effort on 30 September 2026, including reasoning and council. The bounded comparison completed, but human semantic verdicts remain pending; this rollout is not a claim of measured quality superiority. See docs/SOL_UPGRADE_EVALUATION.md.
Provisional demanding tier placement and a distinct developer from the OpenAI demanding models, so a demanding round is not pinned to one vendor.

Provisional escalation placement: the second group of the reasoning and council profiles, never placed for routine, background or research work. Whether it spends premium allowance is an inference_policy route_class decision, not one this file makes.

Provisional escalation placement, the last group of the reasoning and council profiles. Placing it last is what makes the escalation bounded: it is reached only when no earlier group is eligible. It is not an automatic candidate for routine, background or research work.

profiles.notes: Interactive chat and tool work. One accepted automatic candidate: Luna at its low default effort, in the profile's only group. There is no automatic fallback group, so a request Luna cannot serve is refused with a truthful unavailable/capacity result instead of being answered by a model that was never evaluated for this workload. Premium is never auto-considered here: routine and background stay routine unless the account explicitly selects a premium model. An exact manual selection is still honoured and still has to clear qualification, capability, entitlement and budget checks.

Titles, extraction and basic summaries use this routine-funded pool, which now carries the same single accepted automatic candidate as routine: Luna at low effort, with no automatic fallback group. A background job Luna cannot serve is refused rather than silently rerouted. Substantial background reasoning and consolidation use the separate reasoning profile under the same account limits.

Hard interactive work. The demanding group is the normal choice; the escalation group is reached only when no demanding candidate is eligible, so the automatic climb is bounded by two steps and remains subject to the account's premium_routing capability and premium budget.

Ordinary source synthesis remains accessible on routine capacity; complex analysis is classified as reasoning. The single accepted automatic candidate is Luna at low effort, at this profile's larger comparable output floor. The demanding and escalation groups are removed, so there is no automatic premium candidate and no automatic fallback: an unavailable or ineligible Luna yields a truthful unavailable/capacity result. allow_premium stays true, but with no premium model in the group it now admits no automatic premium candidate; a manually selected premium route still requires account eligibility and funding.

Provisional council pool. Role preferences are honored within the diverse group after qualification and budget checks; exclusions and actual-result checks preserve developer independence. Escalation remains bounded.
